unit.why: A first-person memorate, told by the tsaddik: as an eight-year-old at his grandfather's Seder he saw the departed Maggid R. Dov Ber appear.

stories.start_quote: והנה גם כשהיה קטן היה לו מדרגות גדולות
stories.end_quote: והוא מדרגה יותר גדולה מגילוי אליהו
stories.summary_en: As an eight-year-old at his grandfather the Maggid's Seder, the tsaddik saw a figure revealed while the grandfather spoke Torah in the name of his teacher R. Dov Ber; the boy took it for Elijah, but the grandfather explained it was R. Ber himself, a higher degree than a revelation of Elijah.

tags.why: The scene is Passover night at the Seder.

quotes: וראיתי כי בא ונתגלה אליו ז"ל
tags.why: The boy sees the departed master appear while awake.

tags.why: A supernatural revelation of R. Dov Ber's soul is described.
The child perceives a presence that others at the table do not see.

quotes: וראיתי כי בא ונתגלה אליו ז"ל
tags.why: A dead tsaddik's soul appears to the grandfather.
Elijah is invoked only as the boy's mistaken identification of the figure.
The tsaddik's grandfather is a central character.

quotes: בני לא אלי' הוא זה רק מורי ר׳ ר׳ בער ז"ל
tags.why: The figure turns out to be R. Ber, not Elijah.

quotes: ד״ת בשם מורו הק' מהד״ב ז״ל
tags.why: The grandfather's bond with his teacher, the Maggid of Mezeritch, draws the teacher's appearance.

quotes: אמר אא״ז ז"ל ד״ת בשם מורו
tags.why: Words of Torah are delivered at the Seder.
The tale is framed as told by the tsaddik himself.
